newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end firmer as yen slips.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end firmer as yen slips.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures settled barely firmer on Tuesday, rising from early lows as the dollar crawled higher late in the day, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from flat to two yen per gram firmer.
Most-active benchmark February was up one yen at 1,382 yen.
Traders tended to hold a slightly bullish stance towards yen-based gold futures, taking the view that spot gold has reached a near-term floor and the yen will stay weak against the dollar.
Spot gold was quoted at $350.30/60 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $349.75/350.25 in New York on Monday.

"In gold futures, private investors were slightly on the buying side, although activity was limited ahead of the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committe) meeting later today," one trader said. It was widely expected that the FOCM would make a 25 basis point rise in the federal funds rate.
"The impact on spot gold may be muted if the Fed raises it by 25 basis points. Gold could benefit if a 50 basis point rise takes place and U.S. financial markets fall," the trader said.
Silver futures ended higher buoyed by strong bullion prices, while platinum and palladium futures were mostly easier, trailing dips in the New York overnight market.

In the palladium futures market, private investors built fresh shorts, while trade houses bought futures and sold spot palladium in arbitrage. Japanese traders continued to wait for information from the Russian export agency as to when Japan-Russia contract talks will he held.
Palladium futures ranged from two yen to seven yen per gram weaker. Benchmark February was off two yen at 568 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from five yen per gram lower to one yen up, with benchmark February ending flat at 1,465 yen.
Benchmark February silver was up 0.7 yen at 205.0 yen per 10 grams.--Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
